wire.headline: Utility Firm Reports Revenue Rise Amid Profit Drop and Job Cuts
sentences: Revenue rose 7% year on year to 4.26bn GBP for the quarter to 30 September.
The company plans 850 job cuts, which represents about 6% of the workforce.
Two gas plants are scheduled to close by March 2027, with one located in Wales and the other in Kent.
CEO Marian Holt stated that cost pressure is sharper than expected.
Ofgem has opened an investigation into the company's billing system.
The dividend was held at 12.4p a share.

ND.headline: Energy firm announces 850 job cuts and faces regulatory scrutiny

sentences.text: The company reported that its pre-tax profit fell by 12% to 310m GBP.
The firm plans to cut 850 jobs, which represents about 6% of its workforce.
A Kestrel Securities analyst noted that the job cuts will save 90m GBP a year.
The union Unite is set to ballot its members on taking industrial action.
The Kent plant employs 410 staff and has left the local supply chain exposed.
The MP for Deeside has asked for an urgent meeting with the company.
Since 2024, 1,200 staff have left under a voluntary scheme.
Ofgem is scheduled to report preliminary findings by the end of 2026.
Shares in the company closed at 268p, down 11p.
A customer group logged 3,400 billing complaints in a six-month period.
Talks with unions are set to start on 4 November.
In 2023, Ofgem fined the company 1.8m GBP over billing issues.
The company stated there will be no compulsory redundancies before January 2027.
Kestrel Securities cut its price target to 240p from 290p.
The company employs 4,800 staff in the UK.
